name: Dante completes the Divine Comedy
summary: Dante Alighieri, exiled from Florence, completes the Paradiso shortly before his death in Ravenna. The 14,233-line vernacular Tuscan poem encompasses scholastic theology, contemporary Florentine politics, and the entire moral cosmology of medieval Christendom.

_quarry.structural_significance: Single most influential literary work to fix a Romance vernacular as a vehicle for high culture; Dante's Tuscan becomes the basis of modern standard Italian. Establishes the model of personal vernacular epic that runs through Petrarch, Boccaccio, and Italian Renaissance literary culture.
